rows.name: Aurablade
rows.old:
⚔ AURABLADE — MECHANICAL CORE (PHASE 1.5)

Emotion is not flavor text.
Emotion is a resource.

🔥 Burn — What It Is (Plainly)

Burn represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Burn is not a die pool.
Burn is a state track that unlocks power and risk.

You do not “spend” Burn.
You enter Burn states, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Gain Burn (Concrete Triggers)

You gain 1 Burn when any one of the following occurs:

Universal Burn Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You force a defense check using an Aura feature

  • You escalate without pause (GM-flagged high-risk continuation)

  • You remain in the same Aura for too long without stabilizing

⚠️ Limit:
You bank at most 2 Burn a round from landed hits; each Aura action adds 1, and a subclass may say otherwise.

Burn rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Burn States (Explicit Bands)

Burn is divided into three states.

🔹 Burn 0–1 — Controlled

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Burn 2–3 — Engaged

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit mechanical effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Burn 4+ — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

At this state:

  • Aura effects intensify

  • GM is authorized to:

    • Trigger backlash

    • Apply collateral

    • Force Aura collapse on a bad roll or narrative beat

This is the danger state.

🔥 What Happens at Backlash (Clear, Bounded)

When backlash triggers (GM discretion or subclass feature):

One of the following occurs (GM chooses or rolls):

  • You take psychic or sephirotic damage

  • You suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on your next attack or save

  • Your Aura collapses (you drop to Burn 0)

  • A narrative consequence occurs (fear, escalation, attention)

Aurablades are not punished randomly.
They are punished predictably.

💠 AURA STATES — EXPLICIT MECHANICAL EFFECTS

Each Aura grants:

  • A passive effect

  • Engaged Burn effects

  • Overheated Burn effects

These are not manifestations.
They are combat permissions.

🔥 FURY — Escalation & Force

Theme: Press harder. Break lines.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to damage rolls with melee weapon attacks

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

When you hit with a melee attack:

  • Deal +tier damage

  • You may push the target 1 square or cleave a second creature within reach (once per turn)

You may also:

  • Ignore roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one attack per turn

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target must succeed on a Violence defense or be knocked prone

  • Your attacks deny reactions until the start of your next turn

⚠️ Risk:

  • On a missed attack, GM may trigger backlash

Fury trades control for dominance.

🛡 RESOLVE — Defense & Refusal

Theme: Stand firm. Make removal expensive.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to Guard while you have not moved this turn

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

You may:

  • Halve the next hit you take before the start of your next turn

  • Ignore forced movement up to 2 squares

Additionally:

  • Reaction strikes against you roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Automatically succeed on one Violence, Body, or Intrigue check per round

  • Lock your position: enemies cannot move you at all

⚠️ Risk:

  • When damage is fully negated, backlash may occur

Resolve dares the world to try harder.

🤍 MERCY — Protection & Restraint

Theme: Prevent loss. Redirect harm.

Passive (Always On)

  • You may choose to deal nonlethal damage without penalty

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

Once per round, when an ally within 2 squares takes damage:

  • Reduce that damage by tier

  • You may redirect it to yourself

You may also:

  • Automatically stabilize a creature you touch

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Prevent an ally from dropping below 1 Integrity (once per round)

  • Convert a failed Last Stand check into a success

⚠️ Risk:

  • Preventing death may trigger backlash or Aura collapse

Mercy delays consequences — it does not erase them.

🕳 DREAD — Suppression & Collapse

Theme: Remove hope. End momentum.

Passive (Always On)

  • Enemies within 1 square suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on fear and nerve checks (GM adjudication)

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

On hit:

  • Target must make a Soul defense or be Shaken until the end of its next turn

  • Target cannot take reactions

You may also:

  • Suppress one buff or inspiration effect (GM adjudication)

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target suffers roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on all saves until the start of your next turn

  • Nearby enemies must make a defense check or hesitate (lose movement or reactions)

⚠️ Risk:

  • Collateral fear or narrative fallout is likely

Dread does not kill bodies.
It kills belief.

🔄 Changing Aura (Explicit Rule)

You may change your Aura:

  • As a bonus action

  • Or as part of a Soma Break or narrative reset

Changing Aura:

  • Costs 1 Burn

  • Does not clear Burn; Stabilize or Meditate for that

Frequent swapping = control
Deep commitment = power

🧠 How Players Should Think About Aurablade

Ask yourself every turn:

  • “Do I escalate — or stabilize?”

  • “Can I afford another Burn?”

  • “What happens if this goes wrong?”

Aurablades are not forgiving.

They are honest.

🔥 Heat — What It Is (Plainly)

Your heat is your Surge — the same bank every steward fills by rolling 10s. How full it is represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Every class runs hot; the Aurablade is built to live there.
The fuller your Surge, the more your Aura unlocks — and the closer you are to the edge.

Spending Surge cools you.
Holding it lets you ride the band, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Heat Up (Concrete Triggers)

Besides rolling 10s, you gain 1 Surge when any one of the following occurs:

Aurablade Heat Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You use an Aura action

  • You switch your Aura

⚠️ Limit:
You bank at most 2 Surge a round from landed hits; each Aura action adds 1, and a subclass may say otherwise.

Heat rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Heat Bands (Explicit)

Your Surge reads as three bands, scaled to your Surge cap (Tier 1: 4 · Tier 2: 6 · Tier 3: 8 · Tier 4: 10).

🔹 Below half your cap — Cool

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Half your cap or more — Stoked

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit mechanical effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Full — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

rows.old:

Aura States (Fury, Resolve, Mercy, Dread) shape a luminous blade. Spending power builds Burn; at high Burn you gain potency and risk backlash.

rows.name: Aurablade: Vent Surge

rows.name: Blood Hymn (Bad Eden)
rows.old:
The wound is the prayer.

Mode: Martyr

Blood Hymn Aurablades convert suffering into amplification. Where the base class governs Burn and Aura, the Hymn turns each blow into fuel — for cleave, for fear, for irreversible certainty. Played as the operative who runs toward the worst version of the fight on purpose.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Escalation. Your Burn feeds itself. While at Burn 2–3 (Engaged), weapon attacks deal +tier damage and grant +1 Burn (once per turn). At Burn 4+ (Overheated), the bonus scales further.
  • Level 6 — Lifetithe. Convert flesh into certainty. As part of an attack or Aura effect, take self-damage equal to your tier to gain +1 Burn (no action), reroll one damage die, or reclaim a previously expended Aura effect this turn.
  • Level 10 — Crimson Arc. Your violence spills outward. Once per turn, when you hit at Burn 2+, choose another creature within reach and deal half the original damage to them. At Burn 4+ the secondary target takes full damage and both must check against an additional rider.
  • Level 14 — Terror Charge. Fear trails behind you. While at Burn 3+, creatures you hit make a Soul defense or become Shaken; Shaken creatures suffer 3d10 keep lowest 2 on reaction strikes against you and have reduced movement when fleeing. At Burn 4+ nearby allies of your target are also affected.
  • Level 18 — Final Crescendo (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, as a bonus action: enter Burn 4 immediately. For the rest of the turn, all attacks deal maximum damage and you may cleave freely (no once-per-turn limit). Aftermath: your Burn drops to 0 and you suffer severe backlash.

rows.name: Soul-Smith
rows.old:
"Give me time, a fire, and something to hit — and then we'll see."

The Soul-Smith runs a forge that does not much care whether you call it a person or a furnace; it answers to heat and intention either way. Mechanically you ride Burn — a 0→8 heat track that climbs when you or a nearby ally takes a hit (the forge stokes itself on other people's bad days) and banks Surge right alongside it. You spend that Surge on four forge-works, and the hotter you run, the harder they land — right up until the furnace bites back.

The Four Works (spent via Surge)

  • Forge-Weld. Lay hands on the breakage and repair an ally — 1d8 + tier integrity. Stoked (Burn 2–3) ×1.5; Overheated (Burn 4+) ×2, and Overheated also costs you 1d6 Stress, because an open forge has opinions about being grabbed.
  • Atonement Crucible. Cleanse a condition off an ally (two while Stoked or hotter) and temper the wound into armor — they gain DR equal to your tier. The bad thing that happened to them is now load-bearing.
  • Furnace of Renewal. Light the aura: allies within 6 squares heal (Burn-scaled) and share your poison/qliphothic resistance for three rounds. Stand near the fire. It is rude not to.
  • Relic of Rebirth. Forge a ward on an ally — the next hit that would drop them is held at 1. While Overheated, instead reforge a fallen ally back to half integrity (once per fight). The forge does not accept "dead" as a final answer. It considers it a draft.

Vent to cool Burn. Out of combat, Forge Works still does the slow miracles — repairing hexes, purifying corrupted Sparks, restoring ruined regions. Those take time, the way good welds do.

rows.name: Stillheart (Bad Eden)
rows.old:
The calm is the discipline.

Mode: Protector

Stillheart Aurablades hold the aura instead of feeding it. Burn arrives by stillness rather than damage; the doctrine extends safety outward, denies panic to the people you stand near, and refuses disruption when the field starts to fray.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Centered Breath. Reduce Burn gained by 1 per encounter (minimum 0). Once per round when you would gain Burn you may decline. Allies within 2 squares reroll the lowest die on their first check vs fear or charm each scene.
  • Level 6 — Shared Aura. Extend stability outward. While at Burn 1–3, allies within 2 squares gain half your Aura's passive benefit (Fury: +1 dmg once/turn; Resolve: +1 Guard while stationary; Mercy: free nonlethal choice; Dread: reroll the lowest die against fear).
  • Level 10 — Quiet Mind. You and allies within 2 squares are immune to being Shaken and reroll the lowest die on checks against charm, confusion, or fear. At Burn 3+ you may spend your reaction to cancel one fear or charm effect on an ally.
  • Level 14 — Emotional Lock. Your Aura cannot be forcibly changed. As a bonus action, freeze your current Burn level — it cannot increase or decrease until the start of your next turn. At Burn 3+ you may ignore one backlash trigger entirely.
  • Level 18 — Eye of the Storm (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, for 1 minute in a 4 squares radius: Burn does not increase for you or allies; fear, charm, and fear effects are suppressed; ongoing emotional effects pause. After it ends, you gain 1 Burn.

rows.name: Void Edge (Bad Eden)
rows.old:
Entropy has a shape. I cut along it.

Mode: Edge-walker

Void Edge Aurablades cut along the seams of decay. The doctrine suppresses what enemies rely on — buffs, banked rerolls, nerve — and propagates dread into the spaces between people. Played as the operative whose presence makes hope harder to organize.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Null Field. Your blade suppresses their edge. When you hit at Burn 1+, suppress one of the following until the end of the target's next turn: reroll-lowest on attacks, bonus damage, or fear or inspiration effects. At Burn 3+ the target also loses one reaction.
  • Level 6 — Silence of Will. You break focus. Targets you hit roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Clarity hold checks and cannot benefit from rallying or command effects. At Burn 3+, failing a Clarity hold also causes Burn-like fatigue (GM narrative).
  • Level 10 — Dread Cut. Fear propagates. When you hit at Burn 2+, the target saves or is Shaken; nearby enemies save or suffer hesitation (lose movement or reactions). At Burn 4+ fear spreads automatically to one additional creature.
  • Level 14 — Emotional Erasure. Once per round when you hit, remove one beneficial emotional, nerve, or inspiration effect from the target. Bypasses resistance tied to hope or courage. At Burn 4+ the effect cannot be reapplied for 1 round.
  • Level 18 — Final Quiet (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, create a 6 squares zone for 1 minute: nerve cannot rise, inspiration fails, hope or courage buffs do not apply, enemies roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on checks vs fear. Afterward your Burn drops to 0.
